newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SAMPDORIA LOSE GROUND TO JUVENTUS AFTER DEFEAT TO ROMA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SAMPDORIA LOSE GROUND TO JUVENTUS AFTER DEFEAT TO ROMA.

text.p: Second-placed Sampdoria lost ground to league leaders Juventus on Sunday after a 2-1 home defeat to Roma brought their seven match unbeaten run to an abrupt halt.

Goals in each half from Francesco Moriero and Argentina's Abel Balbo accounted for Sampdoria, who badly missed their inspirational captain Roberto Mancini and first-choice goalkeeper Fabrizio Ferron -- both suspended.
Alessandro Del Piero made sure Juve took maximum advantage of Samp's slip-up by scoring both goals, the first from the penalty spot, in his side's 2-1 win over struggling Perugia at Turin.
With 40 points from 20 matches, victory stretched Juve's lead over Samp to five points, with three clubs - Bologna, Inter and Atalanta - tied a distant third on 31 points.

Jesper Blomqvist scored his first goal since joining Milan in the champions' 2-0 win over Bologna at the San Siro -- but the Swede's celebrations were short-lived as a crude tackle two minutes later saw him sent-off.

Inter scored twice in two minutes through Chilean Ivan Zamorano and Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff to earn a 2-2 draw at Lazio, while Atalanta stretched their unbeaten run to 10 matches with a 3-1 win over Vicenza.
In other games struggling Verona beat Fiorentina 2-1, Piacenza edged Napoli 1-0 and Udinese defeated Cagliari 1-0.
Reggiana were playing Parma later on Sunday.
